problem_statement: Module-mapped logging must support registration and mapping, fan out to mapped logs, apply level filtering, fall back to the default log, format messages, and preserve append behavior.
extra_warnings: Use the supplied tests as the acceptance oracle. Do not add, remove, or modify tests or test helpers.

verification.reason: The original statement is too terse to solve without guessing many public names, signatures, configuration settings, and exact behaviors; all missing items can be added as public interface requirements without revealing the implementation.

problems.detail: The statement omits the public package/header and API names that the hidden tests use: sys/log/modlog, modlog/modlog.h, modlog_desc, modlog_foreach_fn, modlog_get, modlog_register, modlog_delete, modlog_append, modlog_append_mbuf, modlog_foreach, modlog_printf, and MODLOG_MODULE_DFLT.

The statement does not specify required observable behaviors: NULL log returns SYS_EINVAL, unknown handle returns SYS_ENOENT, nullable out_desc/out_handle, unique handles, min_level filtering, fan-out to all matching mappings, default mapping fallback, no-mapping success, foreach order, mbuf ownership/freedom, and printf truncation.
Exact values are missing: MODLOG_MODULE_DFLT must be 255, and MODLOG_MAX_PRINTF_LEN must exist and control truncation to MODLOG_MAX_PRINTF_LEN - 1 bytes.
The test configuration relies on syscfg settings MODLOG_MAX_PRINTF_LEN and MODLOG_CONSOLE_DFLT, but the statement does not mention them.

problem_statement_fixed: Module-mapped logging must support registration and mapping, fan out to mapped logs, apply level filtering, fall back to the default log, format messages, and preserve append behavior. Provide a package named sys/log/modlog that depends on the log API and exposes a public header modlog/modlog.h. That header must define struct modlog_desc with fields log, handle, module, and min_level; a typedef modlog_foreach_fn for a callback taking const struct modlog_desc * and void * and returning int; and the functions modlog_get, modlog_register, modlog_delete, modlog_append, modlog_append_mbuf, modlog_foreach, and modlog_printf with signatures int modlog_get(uint8_t handle, struct modlog_desc *out_desc), int modlog_register(uint8_t module, struct log *log, uint8_t min_level, uint8_t *out_handle), int modlog_delete(uint8_t handle), int modlog_append(uint8_t module, uint8_t level, uint8_t etype, void *data, uint16_t len), int modlog_append_mbuf(uint8_t module, uint8_t level, uint8_t etype, struct os_mbuf *om), int modlog_foreach(modlog_foreach_fn *fn, void *arg), and void modlog_printf(uint16_t module, uint16_t level, const char *msg, ...). The macro MODLOG_MODULE_DFLT must equal 255 and identifies default mappings. The package must have an initializer that prepares modlog state during sysinit, and the syscfg settings MODLOG_MAX_PRINTF_LEN (default 128) and MODLOG_CONSOLE_DFLT (default 1) must exist; MODLOG_CONSOLE_DFLT controls whether the initializer registers a default mapping to the console log. modlog_register must return 0 on success, SYS_EINVAL if log is NULL, and SYS_ENOMEM if no mapping space is available; out_handle may be NULL and when provided must receive a handle unique among live mappings. modlog_delete must return 0 for a valid handle and SYS_ENOENT for an unknown handle. modlog_get must return SYS_ENOENT when no mapping with the handle exists; out_desc may be NULL. modlog_foreach must visit mappings in ascending module order, pass each mapping to fn, return 0 if fn completes, and return fn nonzero result if fn aborts. For modlog_append and modlog_append_mbuf, the data buffer or mbuf already contains a struct log_entry_hdr prefix, and the length passed to modlog_append is the body length, not including the header; the facility must forward the entry to the mapped log unchanged. Entries must be written to all mappings whose module matches the entry module. If no exact module mapping exists, entries must be written to every mapping whose module is MODLOG_MODULE_DFLT. If no mapping and no default mapping matches, modlog_append must do nothing and return 0; modlog_append_mbuf must take ownership of the mbuf, free it after attempting all mapped writes even if no mapping matches, and return 0. A mapping with min_level m must discard entries with level less than m. modlog_printf must format the message using varargs and append a LOG_ETYPE_STRING entry whose body is the formatted text; if the formatted body would exceed MODLOG_MAX_PRINTF_LEN minus 1 bytes, only the first MODLOG_MAX_PRINTF_LEN minus 1 body bytes are written, and the entry length excludes the header.
